page: Microsoft Azure E32-8ads_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the EADSv5 server family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz. The server is configured with 8 dedicated vCPUs, derived from 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features a substantial memory capacity of 256.0 GB, which equates to 32.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Additionally, the instance includes 1229 GB of local SSD storage and supports Premium Storage.

In benchmark evaluations, the E32-8ads_v5 demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance, placing in the top 25% of tested servers. Multi-core CPU performance and software compilation tasks fall within the average tier. The memory subsystem exhibits average performance for cached, small-block read operations, but shows weaker performance for large-block read and write operations, placing in the bottom 25%. Database operations, Redis SET performance, and static web serving throughput all register in the average range. For machine learning workloads, the server achieves average text generation speeds on medium-sized models, though prompt processing speeds for those models are relatively weak.

The hardware profile of the E32-8ads_v5 offers high memory density relative to its compute resources, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for workloads that require large memory footprints without needing massive parallel processing power. The inclusion of a 1229 GB local SSD provides high-speed temporary storage, reducing the need for external storage attachments for transient data. This configuration is highly suitable for memory-intensive applications, relational database management systems, caching layers, and data analytics tasks that benefit from a high RAM-to-vCPU ratio.

It is highly suitable for hosting databases, caching layers, and memory-intensive enterprise applications that require significant memory capacity and local storage without requiring high parallel compute scaling.
